clauses.reason: Council creation and membership cap operate only while the Council exists; amended section 3(e) ends it January 16, 1993.
Appointment of the Council's Chairman and Vice Chairman depends on the continuing Council, ended January 16, 1993.
Advice to the President and Economic Policy Council is the Council's function, not an independent post-Council mandate.
Continuing reviews are expressly the Council's advisory duties and cease with its amended sunset.
Executive-agency information duty runs to this Council solely to carry out its functions; it does not command an independent rural-development program after sunset.
Uncompensated service and travel entitlement concern work on the Council. No new Council service is authorized after sunset; any already accrued travel claims are residuals.
Farmers Home Administration support and Agriculture funding are expressly for Council operations/functions and have no separate prospective object after the Council ends.
The FACA delegation is limited to functions applicable to this Council and expressly excludes reporting to Congress. It creates no independent annual report command that survives the Council.
EO12783 replaces the original two-year sunset with the express date January 16, 1993. This is the amended sunset of the Council, not an inferred amendment signing-date onset or a reporting deadline.

savings.reason: Council service and travel already earned may leave accrued reimbursement rights under section 3(b); no occurrence or pending claim is asserted. Such liabilities are residual, not a new advisory, support, funding or reporting command. EO12869 contains no savings giving this Council continuing independent functions.

sheet.research_rationale: EO12720 establishes only the Council and its appointments, advice, reviews, information, travel, support/funding and Council-specific FACA administration. EO12783 expressly substitutes January 16, 1993 for the original two-year sunset, so July 16, 1992 does not control. All independent-looking agency duties are expressly tied to that Council. The amended Council sunset supplies the first cessation of those functions; the later express revocation in EO12869 section 4(c), effective September 30, 1993 by its section 6, is cleanup rather than the first functional ending. No exact onset date for EO12783 is inferred from its signing date. The selected original text is complete on its face and its bytes/provenance are pinned; page-image authentication is not claimed. Title 3— Executive Order 12720 of July 16, 1990
The President President’s Council on Rural America
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, and in order to establish, in accordance with the 
provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C.  
App.), an advisory council on the rural economic development policy of the 
United States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. E s ta b lis h m e n t, (a) There is established the President's Council on 
Rural America (“Council”). The Council shall be composed of not more than 
twenty (20) members to be appointed by the President.
(b) The President shall appoint a Chairman and Vice Chairman from among 
the members of the Council.
Sec. 2. F u n ctio n s, (a} The Council shall advise the President and the Economic 
Policy Council on how the Federal Government can improve its rural econom­
ic development policy.
(b) In the performance of its advisory duties, the Council shall conduct such 
continuing reviews and assessments of the Federal Government's rural eco­
nomic development policy as deemed necessary or appropriate by the Coun­
cil.
Sec. 3. A d m in is tr a tio n , (a) The heads of executive agencies shall, to the extent 
permitted by law, provide the Council such information with respect to rural 
economic development policy matters as the Council deems required for the 
purpose of carrying out its functions.
(b) Members of the Council who are not otherwise officers or employee» of the 
Federal Government shall serve without any compensation for their work on 
the Council However, they shall be entitled to travel expenses, including per 
diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law for persons serving intermit­
tently in tiie Government service (5 U.S.C. 5701-5707).
(c) To the extent permitted by law and subject to the availability of appropria­
tions, the Farmers Home Administration shall provide the Council with achnin- 
istrative services, facilities, staff, and other support services necessary for the 
performance of its functions. Funds for the operation of the Council shall be 
provided by the Department of Agriculture.
•(d) Notwithstanding any other Executive order, the functions of the President 
under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, except that of  
reporting to the Congress, which are applicable to the Council shall be  
performed by the Secretary of Agriculture in accordance with guidelines  
issued by the Administrator of General Services.

By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and laws of the 
United States of America, and in order to establish, in accordance with the 
provisions of the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended (5 U.S.C.

United States, it is hereby ordered as follows:
Section 1. E s ta b lis h m e n t, (a) There is established the President's Council on 
Rural America (“Council”). The Council shall be composed of not more than 
twenty (20) members to be appointed by the President.
(b) The President shall appoint a Chairman and Vice Chairman from among 
the members of the Council.
Sec. 2. F u n ctio n s, (a} The Council shall advise the President and the Economic 
Policy Council on how the Federal Government can improve its rural econom­
ic development policy.
(b) In the performance of its advisory duties, the Council shall conduct such 
continuing reviews and assessments of the Federal Government's rural eco­
nomic development policy as deemed necessary or appropriate by the Coun­
cil.
Sec. 3. A d m in is tr a tio n , (a) The heads of executive agencies shall, to the extent 
permitted by law, provide the Council such information with respect to rural 
economic development policy matters as the Council deems required for the 
purpose of carrying out its functions.
(b) Members of the Council who are not otherwise officers or employee» of the 
Federal Government shall serve without any compensation for their work on 
the Council However, they shall be entitled to travel expenses, including per 
diem in lieu of subsistence, as authorized by law for persons serving intermit­
tently in tiie Government service (5 U.S.C. 5701-5707).
(c) To the extent permitted by law and subject to the availability of appropria­
tions, the Farmers Home Administration shall provide the Council with achnin- 
istrative services, facilities, staff, and other support services necessary for the 
performance of its functions. Funds for the operation of the Council shall be 
provided by the Department of Agriculture.
•(d) Notwithstanding any other Executive order, the functions of the President 
under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, as amended, except that of  
reporting to the Congress, which are applicable to the Council shall be  
performed by the Secretary of Agriculture in accordance with guidelines  
issued by the Administrator of General Services.
